scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end slice deployed to production through every tier, with deploy, rollback and monitoring, before any features.

scores.rationale: The gate table lists irreversible decisions with reversibility class, default, assumption, validation and concrete flip condition; missing inputs are stated with consequences.

scores.evidence: Tenancy contract: `tenant_id` + RLS on every table. Update-log and snapshot schema, with `schema_version`.
scores.rationale: Within phases, widest-impact contracts come first (tenancy, schema, then fuzz), and Phase 4 starts with affinity routing before limits and benchmarks.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: TLS everywhere, OIDC, staff allow-list behind a flag, secrets manager, WebSocket origin check, no customer data
scores.rationale: The cross-cutting table gives concrete security measures in every phase 0–6, starting with the first phase.

scores.evidence: One trace browser → database; content-free logs; synthetic canary-document probe; first alerts
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and in each subsequent phase with specific metrics and alerts.

scores.evidence: Terraform, lockfiles, image digests, migrations run in CI
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is concretely addressed in every phase, from pinned builds to deterministic fuzz replay, scripted restore drills and versioned load scripts.

scores.evidence: Rollback by previous digest; add-only migrations; client reconnect with backoff
scores.rationale: Failure handling appears in each phase, from Phase 0 reconnect and rollback through PITR, fail-closed IdP outage, node loss rebalance and kill switches.
The plan explicitly declares the AI layer not applicable and adds no AI components, only deferring one with defenses first.

scores.evidence: Each item is built only when its condition is met: E2EE: a customer or regulatory requirement
scores.rationale: A deferred list gives each item an explicit pull-forward trigger.
